text: All the Key Hotels in Germany: The Full 2025 Selection Restaurants Hotels Travel Guides Magazine My Lists Restaurants Hotels MICHELIN Guide Plus Travel Guides Best-of Guides Magazine MICHELIN Guide Ceremony Contact us Subscribe to newsletter Booking partnership with OpenTable Booking partnership with Resy USA - English - USD Travel 3 minutes 08 October 2025 All the Key Hotels in Germany: The Full 2025 Selection The MICHELIN Guide announces top honors for German hotels in 2025. Hotels Editor's Pick MICHELIN Keys Germany Berlin Share The MICHELIN Guide's list of the most outstanding hotels in the world has been updated for 2025, and Germany's refresh includes a baker's dozen of new Keys. Like MICHELIN Stars, these accommodations stand out for their excellence across five distinct categories , as confirmed by our hard-working Inspectors. Germany's top-rated accommodations show off a varied landscape of rolling forested hills and dramatic mountain ranges. Berlin's dynamic cityscape features cutting-edge design perched on Prussian-era boulevards, complemented by a carefully considered approach to architecture. Read on for hotel highlights or jump directly to the list here . Browse by highlight or distinction: The Icons The Transformation of Berlin The Importance of Location All the Three Keys All the Two Keys All the One Keys Hotel Bareiss is a family-run, five‑star‑superior resort in the Black Forest. © Hotel Bareiss Germany's Three-Key Hotels All six 3-Key properties in Germany have confirmed their award this year. Two of them are located in Baiersbronn in the heart of the Black Forest ( Hotel Bareiss , Hotel Traube Tonbach ), two in Hamburg ( Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten , the Fontenay ), and two in Bavaria ( Schloss Elmau , Seehotel Überfahrt ). See more: The ins and outs of all our Three Key hotels in Germany Once a women's prison, Wilmina is a tranquil enclave in Berlin's busy center. © Wilmina Hotel The Transformation of Berlin Berlin is a melting pot of history, culture and architecture. While many historic buildings were destroyed in World War II, many managed to survive. This is what makes the Key hotels in the German capital so special - they were converted from historic buildings that were originally post offices ( Hotel Telegraphenamt ), private homes ( Patrick Hellmann Schlosshotel ) or even prisons ( Wilmina Hotel ) from the 19th century. New additions among the Key hotels in Berlin are the legendary Hotel Adlon Kempinski and Hotel Zoo Berlin . See more: Inside Wilmina, Berlin's Former Prison Turned One Key Hotel Read also: Historic Gems: 7 Storied Key Hotels in Berlin Set amid the dramatic Alps, Kulturhof Stanggass is known for its cutting-edge construction. © Kulturhof Stanggass The Importance of Location Fjords, Lake Chiemsee, nature parks and castle ruins: at these coveted addresses, location plays a major role in the appeal. From sunset on the lakefront to sweeping alpine panoramas, the newest MICHELIN Key hotels in Germany combine exceptional architecture, luxury, and service with an unrivaled address. See brand-new Keys like Schlosshotel Münchhausen , Hotel Dollenberg , and Hotel Gut Immenhof for proof. Warm, personalized service and made-to-order breakfast define your stay at Villa Sonnenhof. © Villa Sonnenhof.
